svg.title: The VD55G1 module on a narrow flex: three options, to scale
svg.desc: Top views at 4 pixels per millimetre. Today: the ST CAM-5G1 module on the 30 by 35 mm P-Board, with a Raspberry Pi 5 camera cable 11.5 mm wide, flaring to 16 mm at its 15-pin end. Options A, B and C put the module on a small polyimide pad over its 30-pin BM28 socket, followed by a 5.5 mm wide tail drawn 120 mm long. A ends in a 16 mm wide paddle with regulators, an oscillator, a level shifter, GPIO pads and 15 contacts at 1.0 mm pitch. B ends in an 11.5 mm wide paddle with the same parts and 22 contacts at 0.5 mm pitch. C ends in a 6.6 mm wide tab with 20 contacts at 0.3 mm pitch, plugged into a separate adapter board that carries the parts and a 15-pin socket. Pin assignments are in docs/vd55g1-flex.md, not in this picture.
svg.text: The VD55G1 module on a narrow flex, to scale
The P-Board (30 × 35 mm) adapts the module to a 22-pin socket; the Pi cable is 11.5 mm wide, 16 mm at the 15-pin end, 200 mm long
A. Straight into the ESP32-P4X (or a Raspberry Pi 4): 15-pin end
LDOs, 24 MHz oscillator, I²C level shifter and GPIO pads on the far end; nothing but the module at the eye
B. Raspberry Pi 5 / Zero pinout: 22-pin end
The same parts on a narrower end; plugs into a Pi 5, or into the ESP32-P4X with the 22-to-15-pin cables you have
C. Narrowest: a bare 20-pin end, everything else on the board it plugs into
Bench: a small adapter board to the ESP32-P4X. Head: the serializer board or a custom carrier takes the flex directly
50 mm (1 mm = 4 px). Tails drawn 120 mm; flex ~0.1–0.15 mm thick
